## Fatal findings

1. `ex-products-in-a-poset-are-infima` — Example assertion

The Example says “the identity of the domain of any parallel pair is both an equalizer and a coequalizer.” This is false. For \(f=g:x\rightrightarrows y\), \(1_x\) is the equalizer, but \(1_y\) is the coequalizer. Indeed, the item’s own step 2.1 states exactly that. In the two-element poset \(x<y\), \(1_x:x\to x\) is not even correctly typed as a coequalizer, which must have domain \(y\). The cited definition likewise specifies a coequalizer as \(q:B\to Q\). [Item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-products-in-a-poset-are-infima.md:27), [dependency](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-equalizers-and-coequalizers.md:31).

Severity: **fatal** — the displayed Example assertion is false and contradicts its verification.

2. `thm-top-is-complete-and-cocomplete-and-its-underlying-set-functor-preserves-both` — `[F2]`, used in steps 1.1, 1.2, and 2.1

`[F2]` attributes the characteristic universal properties of initial and final topologies to `def-initial-and-final-topology`. That dependency does not establish those properties; it explicitly says they are “the subject of the next item” and “proved in the next item rather than built into the definitions.” The actual characteristic equivalences occur in `thm-initial-and-final-characteristic-properties`, claims 2 and 4. Steps 1.2 and 2.1 rely directly on those iff statements to prove continuity of the mediating maps. [Item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-top-is-complete-and-cocomplete-and-its-underlying-set-functor-preserves-both.md:41), [cited definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-initial-and-final-topology.md:98), [actual theorem](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-initial-and-final-characteristic-properties.md:49).

Severity: **fatal** — load-bearing inaccurate citation; the theorem is true, but the cited fact does not license its proof.

3. `ex-pullback-in-top` — `[F2]`, used in steps 1.1 and 1.2

`[F2]` says `def-product-topology` proves that a map into \(X\times Y\) is continuous exactly when its coordinate maps are continuous. The cited definition only constructs the product topology and explicitly says its characteristic property belongs to “the next item.” The iff is instead stated in `thm-product-universal-property`, claim 2. Both existence and continuity of the pullback mediator use the overstated fact. [Item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-pullback-in-top.md:44), [cited definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-product-topology.md:122), [actual theorem](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-product-universal-property.md:44).

Severity: **fatal** — load-bearing inaccurate citation.

4. `thm-rmod-is-complete-and-cocomplete` — `[F3]`, used in steps 1.3 and 2.1

`[F3]` claims that `def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules` supplies a free module on every set with the unique linear-extension property. The dependency only defines a basis and says that a module possessing a basis is free:

> “A subset \(B\subseteq M\) is a basis if every element … has a unique expression … A module possessing a basis is a free \(R\)-module.”

It neither constructs \(R^{(S)}\) nor proves the extension property. Consequently the existence of the free module in step 1.3 and the unique extension used to prove the coproduct universal property in step 2.1 are unsupported. [Item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/thm-rmod-is-complete-and-cocomplete.md:49), [dependency](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-generated-cyclic-finitely-generated-and-free-modules.md:37).

Severity: **fatal** — inaccurate citation and missing load-bearing construction; cocompleteness is not established by the written proof.

5. `ex-the-empty-set-is-the-product-of-the-large-family-of-all-sets` — `[F1]` and step 2.1

The Given is a proper-class-indexed discrete diagram, but `[F1]` cites `def-products-and-coproducts`, whose domain is an indexed family \((A_i)_{i\in I}\); its dependency defines an indexed family only when “\(I\) [is] a set.” Thus `[F1]` silently extends a set-indexed product definition to a proper-class-indexed diagram. The verification does prove terminality among the relevant class of cones, but the cited product definition does not license calling that large-diagram limit a product without the domain extension. [Item](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/ex-the-empty-set-is-the-product-of-the-large-family-of-all-sets.md:33), [product definition](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-products-and-coproducts.md:26), [indexed-family scope](/Users/ianx/Projects/prestige-math-library/items/def-indexed-family.md:35).

Severity: **fatal** — inaccurate citation with a changed domain, precisely from set-sized to proper-class-sized indexing.
